reasoning: Recent high-quality polling in the last 45 days consistently shows Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff with a mid-single to high-single–digit lead over Republican Mike Collins, with individual polls ranging from roughly D+4 to D+13 and a polling average around D+6 statewide.[1][3][4][5][7][12][13] Georgia’s Cook Partisan Voting Index remains slightly Republican-leaning at R+3 statewide, but current polling indicates the Senate race margin is best described as roughly **D+6–7** at this point in the cycle, with no fresh presidential general-election polling in this window to define a clear presidential margin.[1][3][4][5][7][12][13]

sources.name: AARP (reported by AARP, The Hill, Newsweek)
sources.details: AARP/Fabrizio Ward & Impact Research poll of 1,060 likely voters finds Ossoff 52% vs. Collins 43%, a D+9 margin in the Georgia Senate race.

sources.name: Wick Research (reported by Daily Signal, Newsweek, AJC)
sources.details: Wick Research poll of 1,175 likely voters shows Ossoff 46.7% vs. Collins 42.9%, a D+3.8 margin in the Georgia Senate race.

sources.name: Fox News (reported by USA Today, AJC, Newsweek)
sources.details: Fox News poll of Georgia registered voters finds Ossoff 56% vs. Collins 43%, a D+13 margin in the Senate race.

sources.name: PollsMax
sources.details: PollsMax aggregation of seven Georgia Senate polls reports a statewide polling average of 48.5% D vs. 42.4% R, giving Ossoff a D+6.1 lead over Collins.

sources.name: The Hill
sources.details: The Hill write-up of the AARP Fabrizio Ward/Impact Research survey highlights Ossoff leading Collins 52%-43%, a D+9 margin, with the lead outside the ±3% margin of error.

sources.name: Newsweek (AARP poll analysis)
sources.details: Newsweek’s coverage of the AARP poll notes Ossoff ahead 52%-43% (D+9) and discusses demographic patterns and enthusiasm gaps in the Georgia Senate race.

sources.name: Newsweek (Wick and Fox coverage)
sources.details: Newsweek article on Georgia’s Senate race cites the Wick poll showing Ossoff at 46.7% vs. Collins at 42.9%, a D+3.8 margin, and references a Fox poll with a D+13 lead.

sources.name: Atlanta Journal-Constitution
sources.details: Atlanta Journal-Constitution report on Georgia’s top races notes a Wick poll showing Ossoff leading Collins 47%-43%, approximately D+4, with around 10% undecided.

sources.name: Roll Call
sources.details: Roll Call’s ‘At the Races’ column highlights the AARP Fabrizio Ward/Impact Research survey finding Ossoff with a 9-point lead over Collins in the Georgia Senate contest.

sources.name: Cook Political Report PVI (via Crystal Ball reference)
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s Partisan Voting Index lists Georgia as R+3 statewide, indicating the state votes about 3 points more Republican than the national average in recent presidential elections.
sources.date_range: As of mid-2020s (structural index, not a poll)
